tasks.description: Add abstract `copy()` method to `Piece` and implement it in all 6 concrete subclasses. `King.copy()` and `Rook.copy()` must preserve the `hasMoved` boolean. Other pieces (`Bishop`, `Knight`, `Queen`, `Pawn`) return a new instance with the same owning `Player`. Signature: `public abstract Piece copy();` on `Piece.java`. Each subclass overrides it. No changes to constructors or other methods.

Rewrite `Board.getCopy()` to produce a true deep copy. Allocate a new `Square[height][width]` array, create fresh `Square(y, x)` instances for each cell, and call `piece.copy()` (from T01) for each non-null piece. The new `Board` constructor must rebuild the internal white/black piece lists from the copied squares. After the change, mutating the copy's squares must have zero effect on the original board. Do NOT touch `Board.executeMove` in this task.

Fix castling in `PossibleStandardKingMoves`. The current `getLeftEmpty()` and `getRightEmpty()` methods are logically broken (De Morgan inversion, see design doc for analysis). Replace them with a single helper `canCastleToward(int direction)` that walks from the king's file toward the board edge: every square between king and rook (exclusive of both) must be empty, and the first piece encountered at the board edge must be an unmoved `Rook`. Remove the separate `getRookLeft`/`getRookRight`/`getLeftEmpty`/`getRightEmpty` methods if they become unused. Keep the existing `canCastleLong`/`canCastleShort` public surface that calls the new helper. Do not add check-through-castling validation here; that belongs in the filter (T06).

Implement en passant generation in `PossibleStandardPawnMoves.possibleMoves()`. The logic: if this pawn is on the en passant rank (y=4 for white, y=3 for black with 0=white back rank), and the last `Move` in the history was a pawn that moved exactly 2 ranks, and that pawn landed on the same rank and an adjacent file (x +/- 1), then add the diagonal target square (one forward, one sideways toward the enemy pawn) to the returned list. Use the `Move` object's start/end coordinates and the stored `pieceType` field to determine eligibility; do NOT call `Pawn.hasMoveJustMovedTwoSquares` or rely on `getStart().getPiece()` post-commit. The target square is added to the normal `List<Square>` return; en passant is identified at execution time in `Board.executeMove` (T05), not here.

Add en passant capture detection to `Board.executeMove`. After the normal move execution, detect en passant: if the moved piece is a `Pawn`, and the move is diagonal (`start.getX() != end.getX()`), and the destination square was empty before the move (no captured piece), then remove the opponent's pawn from the square at `(start.getY(), end.getX())` and update the piece lists accordingly. This detection-at-execution-time approach eliminates the need for an `EnPassantMove` subclass. Be careful to check the empty-destination condition BEFORE `executeMove` modifies the board, or use the move's capture flag.

Implement check-legality filtering in `StandardChessRuleset.getLegalSquares`. Currently this method delegates directly to `getSudoLegalSquares`. Change it to: (1) get pseudo-legal squares, (2) for each candidate, deep-copy the board via `board.getCopy()`, simulate the move on the copy via `boardCopy.executeMove(new Move(sourceSquare, targetSquareCopy))`, and check `isCheck(boardCopy, movingPlayer, moves)` — if NOT in check, the move is legal. For castling candidates (king moving 2+ files), also: (a) if the king is currently in check, exclude all castling candidates; (b) simulate the king on the intermediate/transit square and verify it is not in check there. A castling move is identified by the piece being a `King` and `|targetSquare.x - square.x| == 2`. The transit square x-coordinate is `square.x + sign(targetSquare.x - square.x)`. Note: when constructing simulated moves on the deep-copied board, use the COPIED board's squares (obtained via `boardCopy.getSquare(y, x)`), not the original board's square references.

Replace `Game.checkForGameEnd` with a new `evaluateGameEnd()` method and add all supporting infrastructure. New fields: `protected int halfMoveClock = 0` and `protected Map<String, Integer> positionHistory = new HashMap<>()`. New methods: (1) `evaluateGameEnd()` — after each move, get the next player, check if they have any legal move via `hasAnyLegalMove()`, if no legal moves and in check then checkmate (previous player wins), if no legal moves and not in check then stalemate; then check 50-move rule (`halfMoveClock >= 100`), threefold repetition (compute position key, merge into `positionHistory`, check count >= 3), and insufficient material. (2) `hasAnyLegalMove(Player)` — iterate `board.getPieces(player)`, call `ruleset.getLegalSquares(...)` for each, return true on first non-empty result. (3) `computePositionKey()` — encode active colour + 64-square piece placement + castling rights (king/rook hasMoved) + en passant target file as a compact string. (4) `isInsufficientMaterial()` — detect K vs K, K+B vs K, K+N vs K, K+B vs K+B same colour. Update halfmove clock BEFORE `board.executeMove`: reset to 0 on pawn move or capture (including en passant: pawn diagonal to empty square), increment otherwise. Call `evaluateGameEnd()` AFTER `board.executeMove`. Remove the old king-capture detection. Do NOT modify `getDefaultPlayerName` here; that is handled by T12.

Fix magic constants. In `StandardChessRuleset`: replace hardcoded `8` in `isInBoundsX` with the ruleset's `getWidth()` and in `isInBoundsY` with `getHeight()`. In `PossibleStandardPawnMoves.isOnHomeSquare`: replace hardcoded `y == 1` and `y == 6` with expressions derived from board dimensions (e.g., `1` and `board.getColCount() - 2`, noting the row/col naming swap documented in CLAUDE.md).

Write and expand unit tests for all changed classes. Test classes and cases: (1) `PieceConstructorTest` or new `PieceCopyTest`: verify `copy()` for all 6 piece types; verify `King.copy()` and `Rook.copy()` preserve `hasMoved`. (2) `BoardTest`: deep copy does not share Square instances; deep copy does not share king/rook hasMoved state; en passant capture removes opponent pawn from board. (3) `PossibleStandardKingMovesTest`: castling kingside available; castling queenside available; castling blocked by intervening piece; castling blocked after king moved; castling blocked after rook moved. (4) `PossibleStandardPawnMovesTest`: en passant left; en passant right; en passant not available if last move was not double push; en passant not available after intervening move. (5) `StandardChessRulesetTest`: `getLegalSquares` excludes moves that leave king in check; castling while in check excluded; castling through check excluded; pinned piece cannot move off pin line. (6) New `CheckmateDetectionTest`: Fool's Mate produces checkmate; Scholar's Mate produces checkmate; stalemate detected correctly. (7) New `DrawDetectionTest`: 50-move rule triggers at move 50; threefold repetition triggers; insufficient material K vs K, K+B vs K, K+N vs K. (8) Integration test: play Fool's Mate through `OfflineGame` via `movePiece` and assert `GameState.WHITE_WON_BY_CHECKMATE` (or BLACK depending on setup).

Extend `OnlineGame.backupGameState()` and `restoreGameState()` to cover the new `halfMoveClock` and `positionHistory` fields added in T07. `backupGameState` must save both values (deep-copy the `positionHistory` map). `restoreGameState` must restore both values. These fields are `protected` on `Game`, so `OnlineGame` can access them directly.

Apply i18n to all German display strings. (1) Create `modules/core/src/main/resources/messages.properties` with English translations for all `GameState` enum messages and default player names. (2) In `GameState.java`, replace all German string literals with English equivalents (e.g., `"Kein Spiel gefunden"` -> `"No game found"`, `"Weiß hat durch Schachmatt gewonnen"` -> `"White won by checkmate"`, etc.). Optionally load from the resource bundle, but at minimum replace the hardcoded German strings with English. (3) In `Game.getDefaultPlayerName`, change `"Spieler 0 (Weiß)"` to `"Player 1 (White)"` and `"Spieler 1 (Schwarz)"` to `"Player 2 (Black)"`. This task merges the original T09 (player names) and T12 (i18n) from the design doc.
